extracted.intended_audience: general readers, policymakers, educators, and researchers interested in Iowa education law and book-ban/LGBTQ rights issues
extracted.subtask_description: A factual Wikipedia-style summary of Iowa Senate File 496 (2023), a state law restricting certain school library books and instruction on gender identity/sexual orientation and making related changes to school policies, with legislative history and reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on books depicting sex acts (K–12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Senate File 496 prohibits school libraries from providing books through grades K-12 that depict sex acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page cites this as a central statutory prohibition (see citation [11]). Effects reported include up to 3,400 books being restricted. Portions of the law enforcing this prohibition have been blocked by federal injunctions (e.g., March 25, 2025). Examples of books reportedly affected include classic works (1984, Ulysses), which was raised by a judge when blocking parts of the law as overly broad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on books/instruction about gender identity and sexual orientation (K–6)
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate provision prohibits school libraries from providing books through grades K-6 that depict or give instruction to gender identity and sexual orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is presented distinct from the K–12 sex-act prohibition and applies to both books and 'instruction' through sixth grade. The law's rules for enforcement and definitions have prompted litigation and administrative rulemaking (see Des Moines Register and KCCI citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban on instruction related to gender identity and sexual orientation in K–6 across school types
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill's long title and summary state it prohibits instruction related to gender identity and sexual orientation in school districts, charter schools, and innovation zone schools in kindergarten through grade six.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition explicitly covers multiple types of public schools (district, charter, innovation zone). Litigation and injunctions have questioned and in some cases temporarily halted enforcement of these instructional limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of parents' or guardians' right to make decisions affecting their child
rubrics_metrics.description: The law's long title includes 'establishing a parent's or guardian's right to make decisions affecting the parent's or guardian's child.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a statutory policy goal; page does not provide statutory text elaborating limits or procedures, but indicates the law includes provisions to formalize parental decision-making authority over certain educational matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization for parent/guardian to enroll student in another attendance center within same district under specified circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill authorizes the parent or guardian of a student enrolled in a school district to enroll the student in another attendance center within the same school district in certain specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article quotes this authorization from the long title; the page does not enumerate the 'specified circumstances.' This provision appears intended as a mechanism to accommodate parental choice in response to local instruction/policy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications to student health screenings
rubrics_metrics.description: The long title states the act modifies provisions related to student health screenings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Wikipedia page lists this as one of several administrative/operational changes in the statute but does not provide specifics on what changes to screening procedures or consent are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to school district library program rules and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: The act modifies provisions related to school district library programs (in addition to the substantive prohibitions described elsewhere).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This overlaps with the substantive bans on books; the page references subsequent administrative rulemaking by the Iowa Board of Education (KCCI, Des Moines Register) to implement library rules under the law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications to the educational program for students in various school types
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute modifies provisions relating to 'the educational program provided to students enrolled in school districts, accredited nonpublic schools, and charter schools.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in the long title as a category of change; Wikipedia does not reproduce statutory language but indicates the law affects curricular/educational-program requirements across multiple school sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to duties of education entities and officials
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill modifies 'other duties of school districts, accredited nonpublic schools, the department of education, the board of educational examiners, and the governing boards of charter schools and innovation zone schools.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies institutions whose statutory responsibilities are altered by the act; the article does not detail each duty but flags that administrative roles and oversight responsibilities were changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions regarding competent private instruction and special education
rubrics_metrics.description: The long title notes modifications concerning competent private instruction and special education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists these as affected areas but provides no statutory detail; they indicate the law touches both private instruction (homeschool/competent private instruction regimes) and special education policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement, litigation status, and variation in local compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Portions of the law were blocked via an injunction by a federal judge on March 25, 2025; litigation (e.g., Penguin Random House v. Robbins) was ongoing as of July 2025. Around 170 school districts, including Des Moines Public Schools, have not enforced the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Wikipedia entry summarizes opposition and legal challenges (ACLU of Iowa, Lambda Legal, Penguin Random House, Iowa Safe Schools, Iowa State Education Association). It notes injunctions and court findings (including a judge characterizing parts as too broad), reporting that enforcement has been uneven across districts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical effects and scope of restricted materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The law is commonly referred to as a 'book ban' and up to 3,400 books are known to have been restricted due to the law; courts and commentators have observed the law's broad reach (e.g., reported bans of works like 1984 and Ulysses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This entry synthesizes reported practical outcomes and criticisms recorded on the page: civil-rights groups and publishers challenged the law; media sources documented the scale and some high-profile examples of restricted titles. A judge cited overbreadth when blocking enforcement.
